# Media fixtures

`audio-only.mp4` is 0.1 seconds of synthetic silence encoded as AAC in an MP4
container. It has no video stream and contains no third-party media.

Regenerate with FFmpeg (not required for tests):

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=44100:cl=mono -t 0.1 -c:a aac audio-only.mp4
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,codec_type audio-only.mp4
```

It covers the real-world case where Go's HTTP sniffer reports `video/mp4` for an
audio-only MP4. Synthetic box fixtures additionally cover mixed/video tracks,
truncation, and forged or oversized container headers.

# Export contract fixtures

`export-empty.json` and `export-full.json` are generated by the real Go SQLite
exporter in `TestExportVocabularyGolden`. Fixed IDs/timestamps make regeneration
deterministic. They cover an empty authoritative export, Unicode/HTML-sensitive
text, empty and nested null lists, context-only and dictionary-selected meanings,
and image/audio metadata. The Python worker consumes the same checked-in bytes.

After deliberately changing the export contract, regenerate from the repo root:

```sh
UPDATE_EXPORT_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/storage -run '^TestExportVocabularyGolden$' -count=1
python -m unittest anki_worker.test_export_contract
```

Normal Go tests compare generated output without writing fixtures. Never update
the golden files just to silence an unexplained contract or digest mismatch.
